title: Manifest-signature conformance case
description: One case. Five kinds, because manifest-signature.md has five separable assertions: the strict base64url codec (§4), the RFC 7638 thumbprint (§5), raw Ed25519 verification (§7), the ten-step verification algorithm (§8), and signing (§9). A runner reads `kind` and dispatches. Every kind's payload members are declared at the top level and REQUIRED per kind by the allOf below — declaring them per kind instead would make `additionalProperties: false` reject every valid case, which is the shape docs/spec/conformance/v1/diagnostics/case.schema.json already settled on.

mode.description: base64url only. `decode` reads `input` as a candidate base64url string; `encode` reads it as lowercase hex octets.

input.description: base64url only. Under `decode`, the candidate string verbatim — deliberately unconstrained, since most cases assert a malformed one is refused. Under `encode`, the octets to encode, as lowercase hex with no separators.

jwk.description: thumbprint only. The candidate key. Deliberately unconstrained: §5's thumbprintability rule is what several cases assert, so a key with a numeric member or a missing one must be expressible here.

publicKey.description: ed25519 only. The raw 32-octet public key, lowercase hex. Raw rather than a JWK because this kind tests the primitive, not §5's encoding of it.

message.description: ed25519 only. The signed message, lowercase hex. Empty is a real case — RFC 8032 §7.1's first vector.

signature.description: ed25519 only. The candidate 64-octet signature, lowercase hex.

manifest.description: verify and sign. The document. Unconstrained for the same reason `jwk` is: §8 step 1 rejects manifests that are not objects at all, and the corpus has to be able to carry one.

trustedKeys.description: verify only. The resolved key set (§2), in order. May be empty — §8 step 6 says an empty set is kid-unknown. Entries are unconstrained so a rotation set can carry the unthumbprintable entries step 6 must skip.

privateKey.description: sign only. The private JWK. Unconstrained, so §9 step 1's rejections are expressible.

expect.description: Exactly one of `ok` and `rejected`. `ok`'s shape is the kind's own: the decoded octets as hex or the encoded string (base64url), the 43-character thumbprint (thumbprint), whether verification succeeds (ed25519, where BOTH booleans are successful executions and neither is a rejection), `true` (verify), or the envelope produced (sign).

ok.description: On success. See this object's own description for the per-kind shape.

rejected.description: On refusal: the §10 token. The set is closed at ten; the per-kind allOf below narrows it further, since the pure kinds can only reach two of them.

canonicalizationReason.description: Only alongside `rejected: "canonicalization-failed"`. §10 requires the underlying canonical-json.md §9 reason to be reachable ALONGSIDE the token rather than reported as one of the ten, so the corpus asserts both and neither set absorbs the other.

canonical.description: thumbprint only, on success and optional: the exact octets §5 step 2 hashes, lowercase hex. Hex rather than a string so the case file's own JSON escaping cannot alter what is asserted. Pinning these separately catches a binding that reaches the right digest by the wrong serialization.

expect.description: The primitive returns a verdict; it does not refuse. Both booleans are outcomes, and a `rejected` here would name a token §10 reserves for the envelope.

ok.description: The exact envelope §9 produces. Pinning it is what makes signing reproducible across bindings rather than merely round-trippable within one.
